title: CBC Fundamentals

references.label: Standard clinical hematology laboratory textbooks/manuals (e.g. Henry's Clinical Diagnosis and Management)
CLSI Standards for Clinical Laboratory Practice

summary: The Complete Blood Count (CBC) is a panel that characterizes the cellular components of blood — red blood cells, white blood cells, and platelets — along with derived indices, and is one of the most frequently ordered laboratory tests.
explanation: A standard CBC typically reports: white blood cell (WBC) count and often a differential; red blood cell (RBC) count, hemoglobin (Hb), and hematocrit (Hct/PCV); RBC indices (MCV, MCH, MCHC — see the related formulas) which characterize average red cell size and hemoglobin content; red cell distribution width (RDW), a measure of size variation among red cells; and platelet count. The panel is generated primarily by automated hematology analyzers (see the related equipment entry) using electrical impedance and/or optical light-scatter methods, with manual methods (hemocytometer counts, spun hematocrit, peripheral smear review) available as backup or confirmatory methods. A CBC is a screening/characterization tool — abnormal values point toward further, more specific investigation rather than standing alone as a diagnosis.
